chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd Allah, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Daylami, from 'Ubayd Allah al-Mad'ani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him: 'May I be your ransom, inform me about the saying of Allah, the Exalted:'

Indeed, the penalty for those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive upon earth [with] corruption is that they be killed or crucified or that their hands and feet be cut off from opposite sides or that they be exiled from the earth.
He said: He tied with his hand [indicating four categories], then said: 'O Abu Abdillah, take them four by four.'
Then he said: 'If he waged war against Allah and His Messenger and strove in the earth with corruption, and killed [one person], he is killed.'
And if he killed and took the wealth, he is killed and crucified.
And if he took the wealth and did not kill, his hand and foot are cut off from opposite sides.
If he waged war against Allah and His Messenger and strove in the earth with corruption and did not kill and did not take the wealth, he is exiled from the earth.
I said: 'And what is the limit of his exile?' He said: 'One year. He is exiled from the land in which he acted to another land.'
Then a letter is sent to that city stating that he is exiled, so do not eat with him, drink with him, or marry him until he departs to another.
And a letter is sent to them also with the like of that, so this remains his state for one year.
When that is done to him, he repents while he is humble.

key_terms.تُقَطَّعَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَأَرْجُلُهُمْ: Their hands and feet are cut off

ai.seo_question: What are the four specific punishments for muharib (warrior) in Shia jurisprudence according to Surah Al-Ma'idah?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the four gradations of *hudud* for *al-muharib* by correlating specific criminal acts with the sequential penalties in Quran 5:33, establishing a precise jurisprudential hierarchy. The narration further details the practical implementation of exile (*nafy*), prescribing a one-year period of social isolation where the offender is barred from marriage, trade, and companionship, reflecting the Shia emphasis on both punitive justice and social deterrence.
